name: Tender Frequency — Neural Empathy Art Series
creator: Mirela Tadic-Okonkwo
description: A series of twelve short neural-feed art pieces, each lasting between four and nine minutes, in which the viewer is placed inside the subjective sensory experience of a person from a different tier, age, and augmentation profile going through a mundane moment — washing dishes, waiting for a transit pod, sitting with a sick child. Tadic-Okonkwo sourced the original experiential data from paid volunteers across all tiers and spent three years sculpting each piece to remove identifying information while preserving emotional texture. The series is distributed free on gray-market neural channels.
cultural_impact: Widely cited in social equity discourse as evidence that empathy across tier divides is achievable through shared experience; used without permission in at least two corponation wellness marketing campaigns.
controversy: The Tier 5 episode — sourced from a Spire resident who later withdrew consent — was pulled from distribution and now circulates only on encrypted Shelf channels, making it the most sought-after piece in the series.
story_hooks: A character realizes one of the 'volunteer' experiences in the series is their own — but they never consented and have no memory of being recorded.
The withdrawn Tier 5 episode contains something the Spire resident desperately needs suppressed, and they're willing to pay to find every copy.
A therapist is using Tender Frequency as unauthorized treatment for tier-trauma patients, and the results are extraordinary but legally catastrophic.
